questions: With the +/-0.03 m span, do the outer sensors still give useful readings at the tightest bend, or do they now read near zero at the centre?
Does the reduced signal scale (about 67/m versus 100/m) require a higher kp, and what value worked?
Is there any sign of lag or oscillation from the 0.06 m lead that would justify the 0.04 m lead next?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If the slalom still exits the track, report the max_error at the exit point and whether line loss came before the exit. That will tell us whether to change the lead or the wheel geometry next.

intent: Widen the sensor span from +/-0.02 m to +/-0.03 m using 7 sensors at 0.01 m pitch, keeping the 12 mm footprint so readings overlap. Hold lead (0.06 m), body and drivetrain fixed to isolate the effect. Expected: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, with the slalom finish rate rising above zero. The Integrator should expect the signal scale per metre to drop by about a third and may need kp raised to compensate.
learning: Iteration 0 showed the failures are off-track exits at bends with max_error near the 0.06 m limit, not steering jitter. Sensor reach, not oscillation, is the first limit to test.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced and the evidence is clear. The oval finishes 20 of 20 trials, so the basic sensing and drivetrain work. The s-bend finishes only 5 of 20 and the slalom finishes 0 of 20. Both failures are off-track exits (15 and 20 trials), and the worst max_error values (0.056 on the s-bend, 0.064 on the slalom) reach or pass the 0.06 m off-track limit. The problem is lateral excursion past the sensor reach at bends, not oscillation: steering_oscillation is modest (0.16 to 0.25) and rms_error is small. The current array spans only +/-0.02 m, so when the robot drifts toward the tape edge the outer sensors read little or nothing and the controller loses the line. Change: widen the sensor span to +/-0.03 m with 7 sensors at 0.01 m pitch (the maximum sensor count), keeping sensor_size at 0.012 m so adjacent footprints still overlap on the 25 mm tape. Weights stay linear and scaled to the new span (-2 to +2), so the Integrator will need a somewhat higher kp, because the signal per metre of offset falls from about 100/m to about 67/m. I am keeping the 0.06 m sensor lead and the wheel geometry unchanged so this race isolates the span effect. Expected result: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, with the slalom finish rate rising from zero. If lag then shows up as oscillation, the Integrator's suggested lead reduction to 0.04 m is the next step. Body width stays at 0.12 m because the off-track limit remains 0.06 m for any body_width up to about 0.19 m, so it is not the constraint.
